themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say the answers are non-deterministic and drift more than any action you take; on identity resolution Claude builds a consented device panel because error rates are unknowable where they matter most; on incrementality the platform optimizer reacts to the holdout; on content governance reviewers themselves disagree about what counts as substantiated.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On the semantic context layer today Gemini calls consensus an organizational power struggle disguised as a data architecture problem and Claude says no one has authority to make a definition binding across CRM, finance, and media; the same pattern runs through agentic traffic, where all three build a faster lane so declaring beats spoofing, and through journey orchestration, where channel owners are paid to keep sending.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three build an approved-claim registry and still admit implied claims and shifting legal context escape it; on the semantic context layer ChatGPT warns against collapsing legitimate competing meanings into one universal definition.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say opaque ad platforms and already-trained models cannot show person-level proof, so Gemini expires uploaded lists and Claude falls back on canary identities; on agent execution vendors expose no rollback, and on incrementality the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution every model puts a proxy or gateway in front of martech writes with hard spend and audience caps; the same move appears as a single data egress checkpoint for downstream consent, a shared contact ledger with veto power for journey orchestration, and a declared-agent endpoint for agentic traffic.
